issues.legal_issue: Income generated by exploiting an advantageous use of property may be considered when determining its hypothetical annual rent for rateable valuation, even when the income is a licence fee rather than rent and ordinary letting rent is restricted.
material_facts: The building was let to tenants, and its rateable value had previously been assessed by reference to the rents actually received.

Under an agreement, the owner allowed an advertiser to display a sign on the building’s terrace and received additional income, including consideration for restricting other advertising uses of the building.
The municipal assessing authority increased the rateable value by taking account of the additional income; the owner challenged the increase.
The agreement did not transfer a leasehold interest in the terrace, and the additional payment was characterized as a licence fee rather than rent.
Rent-control restrictions limited the rent chargeable for letting the building, but did not prohibit the owner from charging for the privilege of displaying an advertisement.
issues.conclusion: The additional income could legitimately be considered in determining the annual rent the property might reasonably be expected to fetch, and the enhancement of the rateable value was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 154(1) of the Bombay Municipal Corporation Act, 1888, rateable value is determined by estimating the annual rent for which the property might reasonably be expected to let from year to year, subject to the statutory deduction. The estimate concerns the concrete property in its existing condition and takes account of advantages affecting the rent a hypothetical tenant would offer, including income the tenant could derive by exploiting the property. Whether the arrangement producing that income is a lease or licence, or whether the payment is rent or a licence fee, is not determinative. The Court applied the rating principles discussed in Cartwright v. Sculcoates Union and Robinson Bros. v. Houghton and Chester-le-Street Assessment Committee; it also considered Mahad Municipality v. Bombay S.R.T. Corporation and distinguished Corporation of Calcutta v. Anil Prakash Basu because the relevant hypothetical-tenant argument had not been raised or decided there. The rent restrictions did not prevent charging separately for the advertising privilege.

predicates.property_tax_rateable_assessment: The proceeding concerns determining a property's rateable value for property taxation.
predicates.property_generates_extra_income_from_an_: The property produces income beyond its ordinary letting rent because of an advantage or beneficial use associated with it.
predicates.hypothetical_tenant_could_profitably_exp: A hypothetical tenant could exploit the property's advantage to derive income and would take that opportunity into account when deciding what rent to offer.

issues.definition: When a property-tax rateable assessment concerns property that generates extra income from an advantage a hypothetical tenant could profitably exploit, that income may be considered in estimating the property's hypothetical annual rent.
